entries.knownHazards: The plant contains tremetol, a complex alcohol, and glycosides. These toxins cause a fatal disease known as 'staggers' in cattle. The toxin can be passed through the milk and has caused fatalities in humans who have drunk affected cow's milk[274].
entries.knownHazardsLt: Augale yra tremetolio (sudėtingo alkoholio) ir glikozidų. Šie nuodai galvijams sukelia mirtiną ligą — vadinamuosius „svaigulius“ (staggers). Toksinas pereina į pieną ir yra pražudęs žmonių, gėrusių užkrėstų karvių pieną.

entries.knownHazards: Euphorbia abyssinica has toxic milky sap that causes irritation and blistering if it comes into contact with the skin. The sap can also cause temporary or permanent blindness if it comes into contact with the eyes.
entries.knownHazardsLt: Euphorbia abyssinica turi nuodingų pieniškų sulčių — patekusios ant odos jos sukelia dirginimą ir pūsles. Pakliuvusios į akis gali sukelti laikiną arba nuolatinį aklumą.

entries.knownHazards: The sap contains a latex which is toxic on ingestion and highly irritant externally, causing photosensitive skin reactions and severe inflammation, especially on contact with eyes or open cuts. The toxicity can remain high even in dried plant material[200]. Prolonged and regular contact with the sap is inadvisable because of its carcinogenic nature[214].
entries.knownHazardsLt: Sultys turi latekso — nurijus jis nuodingas, o ant odos stipriai dirgina: sukelia fotojautrumo reakcijas ir stiprų uždegimą, ypač patekęs į akis ar atviras žaizdas. Toksiškumas išlieka aukštas net ir džiovintame augale. Ilgalaikio ir reguliaraus kontakto su sultimis venk — jos kancerogeniškos.

entries.knownHazards: Large quantities of the raw seed may be toxic[159].
entries.knownHazardsLt: Didelis kiekis žalių sėklų gali būti toksiškas.

entries.knownHazards: Although no specific mention has been seen for this species, large quantities of the seed of many species in this genus are thought to be toxic.

entries.knownHazards: Although no specific mention has been made for this species, there have been reports that some members of this genus can cause photosensitivity in susceptible people. Many species also contain oxalic acid (the distinctive lemony flavour of sorrel) - whilst not toxic this substance can bind up other minerals making them unavailable to the body and leading to mineral deficiency. Having said that, a number of common foods such as sorrel and rhubarb contain oxalic acid and the leaves of most members of this genus are nutritious and beneficial to eat in moderate quantities. Cooking the leaves will reduce their content of oxalic acid. People with a tendency to rheumatism, arthritis, gout, kidney stones or hyperacidity should take especial caution if including this plant in their diet since it ca...
entries.knownHazardsLt: Apie šią rūšį konkrečių duomenų nėra, bet pranešama, kad kai kurie šios genties augalai jautriems žmonėms gali sukelti fotojautrumą. Daugelyje rūšių yra ir oksalo rūgšties (būtent ji suteikia rūgštynėms tą būdingą citrininį skonį) — pati savaime ji nėra nuodinga, bet suriša kitus mineralus ir trukdo organizmui juos pasisavinti, todėl gali atsirasti mineralų trūkumas. Vis dėlto daug įprastų produktų — rūgštynės, rabarbarai — turi oksalo rūgšties, o daugumos šios genties augalų lapai yra maistingi ir naudingi, jei valgomi saikingai. Virimas oksalo rūgšties kiekį sumažina. Žmonės, linkę į reumatą, artritą, podagrą, inkstų akmenligę ar padidėjusį rūgštingumą, šį augalą į valgiaraštį turėtų įtraukti ypač atsargiai...

entries.knownHazards: Agave cantala is a species in the genus Agave which contains approximately 257 to 341 species and belongs to the family of the Agavaceae (Century-plant Family). The type species of the genus is Agave americana.

entries.knownHazards: The whole plant is highly toxic due to the presence of the alkaloid colchicine[293 , 310 ]. Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting and abdominal pains are often the first signs of poisoning. The diarrhoea may become severe and haemorrhagic, and can thus lead to metabolic acidosis, dehydration, hypotension and shock. A burning sensation in the throat, stomach and skin may also be an early sign of intoxication. Severe reactions include extensive vascular damage and acute renal toxicity with oliguria and haematuria. The patients may develop convulsions, delirium, muscle weakness, neuropathy and ascending paralysis of the central nervous system. entries.knownHazards: A gross overdose of the root can cause oedema, high blood pressure and congestive heart failure[9, 65]. Do not use during premenstrual syndrome as water retention and bloating occur. If pregnant or have liver cirrhosis use with caution. Avoid using for more than 6 weeks. Excessive quantities may cause headache, sluggishness and potassium depletion [301].
entries.knownHazardsLt: Smarkiai perdozavus šaknies gali atsirasti edema, padidėti kraujospūdis, ištikti staziniam širdies nepakankamumui. Nevartok prieš menstruacijas — sulaiko vandenį, pučia. Esant nėštumui ar kepenų cirozei — atsargiai. Nevartok ilgiau nei 6 savaites. Per didelis kiekis gali sukelti galvos skausmą, mieguistumą ir kalio trūkumą.

entries.knownHazards: The plant, and especially the oil from the seed, contains gossypol. It is believed that this substance, when ingested, causes reduced sperm levels and infertility in men[238 , 254 ].

entries.knownHazards: The ripe seed contains hydrocyanic acid. This toxin can be destroyed by thoroughly heating the seed for at least 3 hours at 150°c[183]. The seed contains saponins[222]. Although toxic, these substances are very poorly absorbed by the body and so tend to pass through without causing harm. They are also broken down by heat so a long slow baking can destroy them. Saponins are found in many plants, including several that are often used for food, such as certain beans. It is not advisable to eat large quantities of food that contain saponins. Saponins are much more toxic to some creatures, such as fish, and hunting tribes have traditionally put large quantities of them in streams, lakes etc in order to stupefy or kill the fish[K].
entries.knownHazardsLt: Sunokusiose sėklose yra cianvandenilio rūgšties. Šį toksiną galima sunaikinti sėklas bent 3 valandas kruopščiai kaitinant 150 °C temperatūroje. Sėklose taip pat yra saponinų. Nors saponinai nuodingi, organizmas juos labai prastai įsisavina — paprastai jie tiesiog praeina nepakenkę. Jie taip pat suyra nuo karščio, todėl ilgas, lėtas kepimas juos sunaikina. Saponinų yra daugelyje augalų, įskaitant ne vieną maistinį, pavyzdžiui, kai kurias pupeles. Didelio kiekio saponingo maisto valgyti nepatariama. Saponinai kai kuriems padarams, ypač žuvims, yra žymiai toksiškesni — medžiotojų gentys tradiciškai juos didelius kiekius berdavo į upelius ir ežerus, kad žuvis apsvaigintų ar užmuštų.
